transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what made me come in is that... the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat. And heavy. Like, I just stopped initiating them. My photography walks, for instance. I usually go every Sunday. I actually shoot on film, 35mm, mostly black and white. There's this little lab downtown that still develops it, run by this older couple, Bob and Martha. They've been in that same storefront since the 80s, I think. Martha always gives me a hard time about my exposure settings, but she makes the best coffee. 

But yeah, I haven't been doing that. Or mentoring the kids at the community center. Even keeping a clean calendar feels like too much, which is bad because I'm an executive secretary, so a messy calendar is basically a cardinal sin in my line of work. My boss, Mr. Davis, he's absolutely obsessed with Outlook color categories. If a zoom link isn't color-coded purple, he acts like the whole network is down. But lately, I just... I don't know, I just can't bring myself to care about the colors or the kids or the camera. It's all just heavy.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things in a similar way?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been pretty steady. My mom used to say I was the anchor of the family, which is funny because my dad was actually in the Navy. He was stationed in San Diego for a while, and we lived in this little house near the base. The soil there was terrible for growing anything, but my mom was determined to have a tomato garden. She'd spend hours out there, just fighting with the dirt. She used this weird fertilizer that smelled like old fish, and the neighbors complained once, but she got these massive beefsteak tomatoes by August. We ate tomato sandwiches for weeks. Just mayo, salt, pepper, and thick slices of tomato on white bread. You really can't beat a good tomato sandwich, you know? The ones you get at the store now, they just taste like water. It's sad, really. But anyway, yeah, I've never really felt this... heavy before. It's all new to me.
Did something stressful happen in your life shortly before this started?

Well, I suppose... yeah. It started about a year and three months ago. My sister, she got really sick, and her behavior just got so unpredictable. I had to step in and take over coordinating all her appointments and her bills and everything. Which reminds me, I really need to call the cable company about her account. They keep sending these final notices, but they're printing them on this neon pink paper. It's the most aggressive shade of pink I've ever seen. It looks like a highlighter exploded in the mail sorting machine. I actually used to collect highlighters when I was in middle school. I had this whole pencil case full of them, different brands, different tip sizes. The chisel tips were the best for making those perfect, straight lines in my history textbook. Mr. Henderson, my history teacher, he hated it when we wrote in the books, but I couldn't help it. I needed the color-coding to remember the dates. The War of 1812 was always yellow. But anyway, yeah, it's been about fifteen months since I had to start managing all her stuff, and that's when things started feeling so flat.
Have you been feeling this way continuously for at least two years?

No, not two years. Like I was just saying, it's been about a year and three months. Right around the time my sister got sick and I had to start handling all her coordination and her bills. I've been doing a lot of it from my desk at work, which is tricky because the filing system there is completely archaic. We still use these manila folders with the metal prongs that always catch on your sleeves and ruin your sweaters. I had this really nice merino wool cardigan, navy blue, that I got on sale at Macy's last winter. It was so soft, but one of those prongs snagged the cuff and pulled a whole thread loose. I tried to fix it myself with a needle and thread, but I don't really have the best eyesight for close-up work anymore. I've been thinking about getting those reading glasses, the ones you can buy at the pharmacy on those little spinning racks. They have some with tortoiseshell frames that look pretty dignified, I think. My uncle Arthur used to wear tortoiseshell glasses, and he always looked like a college professor, even though he just sold insurance. But yeah, no, not two years. Just the fifteen months since I took over my sister's stuff.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of killing yourself?

No, I haven't really had thoughts like that. I mean, I'm tired, and things are heavy, but I don't want to die. I just want to sit in a quiet room for a very long time. Actually, speaking of quiet rooms, they're redoing the breakroom at my office right now, and the noise is just unbelievable. They're ripping up the old linoleum, which I always hated anyway because it was this sickly pale green color, like split pea soup. I tried making split pea soup once in a slow cooker, but I forgot to soak the peas first, and they ended up like little gravel stones. I almost chipped a tooth. It was a back molar, the one that already has a silver filling from when I was twelve. My dentist back then was Dr. Gable, and he always gave out those little sugar-free lollipops after a filling, which I thought was kind of counterproductive, even if they were sugar-free. They tasted like artificial cherry and always made my tongue bright red. But anyway, no, I haven't been thinking about hurting myself or anything like that. Just feeling really worn down.
Because of how you've been feeling, have you been able to keep doing your job?

Well, my work has stayed intact overall, thankfully. I haven't lost my job or anything. But I have noticed I've missed a few calendar details here and there, and I've had to double-check tasks that used to be completely automatic for me. Like scheduling the quarterly review meetings for the VPs. I used to do that in my sleep. Speaking of sleep, I bought this new memory foam pillow last week because my neck was getting so stiff. It's supposed to have this cooling gel layer, but honestly, it just feels like sleeping on a cold slab of dough. I used to make sourdough bread during the pandemic, you know? Everyone was doing it. I had this starter named 'Dough-lores' that I kept alive for almost two years. I'd feed her every morning before I even made my coffee. I had this specific bag of artisanal rye flour I ordered online just for her. But anyway, yeah, work is okay, just takes more effort. I've also pulled back from my photography outings on the weekends, and I stopped mentoring the junior admins. I just don't feel as present or reliable right now, you know? Like I'm just going through the motions.
Would you say this depression has made you unable to carry out your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

Well, like I was just saying, I haven't been completely unable to do things. My work is mostly fine, still intact. I'm just slipping up on some calendar details and having to double-check things that used to be second nature. Which is frustrating, because I've always prided myself on my organization. I actually used to color-code everything in my planner with these specific Japanese gel pens. They're called Pilot G2s, I think? Or no, maybe it was the Muji ones. The Muji ones have that really satisfying click when you take the cap off. I went to the Muji store in the city once, and it was just so minimalist and clean. They had these little acrylic storage boxes that fit perfectly into each other. I bought like six of them to organize my bathroom cabinet, but they ended up just collecting dust because I couldn't decide what to put in them. My sister always teased me about buying containers for things I didn't even own yet. But yeah, outside of work, I'm definitely not doing as much. I haven't been going on my weekend photography walks, and I stepped down from mentoring the newer admins at the office. I just... I don't feel like I can be there for them right now. I'm not reliable enough.
Have you been missing work because of this?

No, no, I haven't been missing work. Like I was saying, my job is still intact overall, so I haven't had to take days off. I still do the commute every single morning. I take the 8:15 train usually, the one that connects through downtown. The seats on that train are this scratchy blue wool material, and they always smell faintly of stale coffee and wet umbrellas. I actually left my favorite umbrella on that train last year. It was a really nice one, a sturdy golf umbrella with a wooden handle shaped like a duck's head. I bought it at this little boutique when I visited Portland a few years back. Portland is just so beautiful in the fall, the leaves are incredible, and they have all these great independent bookstores... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. No, I'm showing up. It's just that I'm missing those little calendar details and having to double-check all those tasks that used to be completely automatic for me. And like I mentioned before, I just don't feel present or reliable enough right now, which is why I stopped my weekend photography outings and the mentoring program at the office. I'm there every day, it's just taking a lot more out of me to stay on track.
Have you lost your appetite?

No, I don't think so. I've been eating about the same as usual. I still make my lunch every day to bring to the office. Usually a turkey sandwich on wheat, maybe some baby carrots. I tried those purple carrots once, from the farmer's market? They look so interesting, but they stain your fingers if you aren't careful. I was chopping them for a stew and my hands looked like I'd been fingerpainting with grape juice. My nephew loves fingerpainting. He's four, and my sister lets him go crazy with the washable paints on their patio. He made me this abstract piece for my birthday that I hung up in my cubicle. It's mostly just brown smears because he mixed all the colors together, but I put it in this nice silver frame anyway. Frames can be so expensive, though, have you noticed? I went to the craft store to get it custom matted and it cost more than my groceries for the week. But yeah, no, my appetite is fine. I'm eating normally.
Have other people noticed that you seem to move or speak more slowly than usual?

No, I don't think anyone has mentioned anything like that. I feel like I'm walking and talking at my normal pace. I actually just had to get these new orthotic inserts for my loafers, though, because the marble floors in the main lobby at work are just brutal on your arches. It's a gorgeous lobby, really stunning art deco design with all this brass detailing and geometric patterns on the ceiling. They actually filmed a movie in our building back in the late 90s. I think it was a thriller with Harrison Ford? Or maybe Richard Gere, I always get those two mixed up in those kinds of movies. I love 90s thrillers, though. They always have that weird blue tint to the lighting and everyone is using those giant, brick-like cell phones with the pull-out antennas. My first cell phone was one of those old Nokias. You could literally drop that thing down a flight of stairs and it wouldn't even have a scratch. I used to play the Snake game on it for hours when I was waiting for the bus. The city just changed all the bus routes in my neighborhood, actually, which is incredibly frustrating because the new map is impossible to read... wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving slow. No, nobody has said my speech or movements are slow.
Have you been neglecting basic things like bathing, getting dressed, or keeping up your home because of how you've been feeling?

No, no, I'm still keeping up with all of that. I shower every morning, and the apartment is clean. I actually just reorganized my entire front closet this past weekend. I color-coordinated all my winter coats and my scarves. I have this one scarf, it's a really soft cashmere blend I got on sale at a department store that went out of business a few years ago. It's a real shame how many brick-and-mortar retail stores are closing down now because of online shopping. I mean, I totally get the convenience of getting things delivered, but the drivers always leave the packages right on the edge of my porch where anyone walking by could just swipe them. 

My neighbor actually had a package stolen last month, and it was a whole set of those expensive copper pots and pans. She was going to use them for her big dinner party. She makes the absolute best sweet potato casserole, she puts those little mini marshmallows on top and broils them until they're perfectly brown. I always burn marshmallows when I try to toast them. I just don't have the patience, I always stick them right in the flame until they catch on fire and turn to charcoal... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, taking care of myself. Yeah, I'm not neglecting anything like that. I'm still getting dressed and keeping the place tidy just fine.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Well, lately, there have been nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up way before dawn, and honestly, I don't even feel tired. I just feel completely ready to go, like I could sit down and answer a hundred emails or reorganize the entire executive appointment list for the month. I actually did that last week, updated the whole calendar system we use. We just switched to this new software, and it's supposed to sync with everyone's phones automatically, but half the time it doesn't update the time zones correctly when the VP travels. He went to Tokyo last month and the calendar kept scheduling his meetings for 3:00 AM local time. 

Tokyo seems like such a fascinating city, though. I watched this documentary about their subway system, and it is incredibly efficient. The trains arrive exactly on the second. Not like the transit here, where you're lucky if the bus shows up within a twenty-minute window. I was waiting in the rain on Tuesday for the express bus, and this car drove by and splashed this huge puddle right onto my slacks. I had to go to the dry cleaners on my lunch break. They have this amazing little bakery right next to the dry cleaners, though, and they make these almond croissants that are just... incredible. They have that powdered sugar on top that gets everywhere if you breathe too hard while you're eating it. I always end up looking like I've been dusted with snow. But anyway, yeah, sleep. I just haven't been sleeping much, but I feel totally energized and ready to work anyway.
During those nights when you sleep only a few hours and still feel energized, do you also feel unusually upbeat or excited?

Yeah, I do. I get these stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, you know? Like everything is just clicking perfectly. Speaking of clicking, I actually just bought one of those mechanical keyboards for my desk at work. The sound the keys make is so satisfying, but Greg in IT says it's too loud. Greg collects vintage typewriters, actually. He brought in this beautiful old Underwood model last week to show me. It weighed an absolute ton, just solid iron. 

My grandfather used to have this huge iron anvil in his garage when I was a kid because he used to do farrier work, shaping horseshoes. Horses are such incredible animals, but I can't really be around them because I'm terribly allergic to hay. My eyes just swell up like balloons. I went on a haunted hayride once in middle school and ended up having to sit in the first aid tent with ice packs on my face the whole night while my friends got to go through the corn maze. Corn mazes are so much fun, except when it gets muddy... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought completely. What did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling upbeat. So, yeah, I'll feel really great and on top of the world, but then the weird thing is, a tiny change—like if someone just reschedules a meeting or moves something on the calendar—can suddenly make me get really sharp with people. It's in a way that honestly kind of surprises me, just how quickly I snap over something so small.
During those energized periods, do you find yourself taking on a lot more projects or getting much more done than usual?

Yeah, absolutely. During those stretches, I just start doing everything. I'll be rebuilding all the work templates, making up these elaborate care plans, emailing relatives I haven't spoken to in months, and reorganizing all my files all at the same time. It's like... if I sit still for even a second, I feel like I'm dropping the ball on something. 

Speaking of balls, I actually signed up for a local bocce ball league last spring. It was supposed to be this fun, relaxing thing on Thursday nights, but some of the guys take it so seriously. There's this one guy, Frank, who brings his own custom-made resin bocce balls in this velvet-lined wooden case. He acts like we're playing in the World Cup or something. I mean, I like sports, but I prefer things you can do at your own pace, like golf. My uncle used to take me golfing when I was a teenager. He had this old set of clubs that were practically antiques. He swore by his 9-iron, said it was the only club he ever really needed. He actually used it to chase a raccoon out of his garage once. The raccoon had gotten into a bag of dog food and made this enormous mess everywhere. Dog food smells so bad when it gets wet, doesn't it? I don't even own a dog, I have a cat, a little tabby named Barnaby. He's very finicky about his food, he'll only eat the pate kind, never the chunks in gravy... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, taking on projects. Yeah, I just do a ton of things all at once, like I can't stop moving or I'll fall behind.

I actually used to color-code everything in my planner with these specific Japanese gel pens. They're called Pilot G2s, I think? Or no, maybe it was the Muji ones. The Muji ones have that really satisfying click when you take the cap off. I went to the Muji store in the city once, and it was just so minimalist and clean. They had these little acrylic storage boxes that fit perfectly into each other. I bought like six of them to organize my bathroom cabinet, but they ended up just collecting dust because I couldn't decide what to put in them. My sister always teased me about buying containers for things I didn't even own yet. But yeah, outside of work, I'm definitely not doing as much. I haven't been going on my weekend photography walks, and I stepped down from mentoring the newer admins at the office. I just... I don't feel like I can be there for them right now. I'm not reliable enough.

doctor.intent: Assess the severity of functional impairment to distinguish a moderate major depressive episode from severe depression and from adjustment disorder with depressed mood and anxiety.
doctor.question: Have you been missing work because of this?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My work has stayed intact overall, but I’ve missed calendar details and had to double-check tasks that used to be automatic. I’ve also pulled back from photography outings and mentoring because I don’t feel as present or reliable.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have been missing work, which directly relates to my functional impairment and how my symptoms are affecting my ability to perform my job.

patient.answer: No, no, I haven't been missing work. Like I was saying, my job is still intact overall, so I haven't had to take days off. I still do the commute every single morning. I take the 8:15 train usually, the one that connects through downtown. The seats on that train are this scratchy blue wool material, and they always smell faintly of stale coffee and wet umbrellas. I actually left my favorite umbrella on that train last year. It was a really nice one, a sturdy golf umbrella with a wooden handle shaped like a duck's head. I bought it at this little boutique when I visited Portland a few years back. Portland is just so beautiful in the fall, the leaves are incredible, and they have all these great independent bookstores... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. No, I'm showing up. It's just that I'm missing those little calendar details and having to double-check all those tasks that used to be completely automatic for me. And like I mentioned before, I just don't feel present or reliable enough right now, which is why I stopped my weekend photography outings and the mentoring program at the office. I'm there every day, it's just taking a lot more out of me to stay on track.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is significant appetite or weight loss, which would support a major depressive episode over adjustment disorder and help gauge severity.
doctor.question: Have you lost your appetite?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of appetite, which is not mentioned in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't think so. I've been eating about the same as usual. I still make my lunch every day to bring to the office. Usually a turkey sandwich on wheat, maybe some baby carrots. I tried those purple carrots once, from the farmer's market? They look so interesting, but they stain your fingers if you aren't careful. I was chopping them for a stew and my hands looked like I'd been fingerpainting with grape juice. My nephew loves fingerpainting. He's four, and my sister lets him go crazy with the washable paints on their patio. He made me this abstract piece for my birthday that I hung up in my cubicle. It's mostly just brown smears because he mixed all the colors together, but I put it in this nice silver frame anyway. Frames can be so expensive, though, have you noticed? I went to the craft store to get it custom matted and it cost more than my groceries for the week. But yeah, no, my appetite is fine. I'm eating normally.

doctor.intent: Assess psychomotor retardation to help distinguish moderate from severe depressive episode, since functional impairment and suicidality do not suggest severe depression and duration/stressor already support depression vs adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Have other people noticed that you seem to move or speak more slowly than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor retardation (moving or speaking more slowly than usual), which is not listed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't think anyone has mentioned anything like that. I feel like I'm walking and talking at my normal pace. I actually just had to get these new orthotic inserts for my loafers, though, because the marble floors in the main lobby at work are just brutal on your arches. It's a gorgeous lobby, really stunning art deco design with all this brass detailing and geometric patterns on the ceiling. They actually filmed a movie in our building back in the late 90s. I think it was a thriller with Harrison Ford? Or maybe Richard Gere, I always get those two mixed up in those kinds of movies. I love 90s thrillers, though. They always have that weird blue tint to the lighting and everyone is using those giant, brick-like cell phones with the pull-out antennas. My first cell phone was one of those old Nokias. You could literally drop that thing down a flight of stairs and it wouldn't even have a scratch. I used to play the Snake game on it for hours when I was waiting for the bus. The city just changed all the bus routes in my neighborhood, actually, which is incredibly frustrating because the new map is impossible to read... wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, moving slow. No, nobody has said my speech or movements are slow.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the depression is severe enough to include marked impairment in basic self-care or household functioning, which would help distinguish major depressive disorder, severe without psychotic features, from moderate major depression or adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been neglecting basic things like bathing, getting dressed, or keeping up your home because of how you've been feeling?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about neglecting basic self-care and hygiene (bathing, getting dressed, keeping up the home), which is not addressed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, no, I'm still keeping up with all of that. I shower every morning, and the apartment is clean. I actually just reorganized my entire front closet this past weekend. I color-coordinated all my winter coats and my scarves. I have this one scarf, it's a really soft cashmere blend I got on sale at a department store that went out of business a few years ago. It's a real shame how many brick-and-mortar retail stores are closing down now because of online shopping. I mean, I totally get the convenience of getting things delivered, but the drivers always leave the packages right on the edge of my porch where anyone walking by could just swipe them. 

My neighbor actually had a package stolen last month, and it was a whole set of those expensive copper pots and pans. She was going to use them for her big dinner party. She makes the absolute best sweet potato casserole, she puts those little mini marshmallows on top and broils them until they're perfectly brown. I always burn marshmallows when I try to toast them. I just don't have the patience, I always stick them right in the flame until they catch on fire and turn to charcoal... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, taking care of myself. Yeah, I'm not neglecting anything like that. I'm still getting dressed and keeping the place tidy just fine.

doctor.intent: Assess whether sleep disturbance is present, which would help distinguish a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder and clarify severity among the depressive diagnoses.
doctor.question: Have you been having trouble sleeping?

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep
target_item.manifestation: There have been nights when I sleep two or three hours, wake up before dawn, and feel ready to answer emails or update appointment lists instead of feeling tired.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my sleep patterns, which corresponds to my symptom of having a decreased need for sleep during my high-energy stretches.

patient.answer:
Well, lately, there have been nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up way before dawn, and honestly, I don't even feel tired. I just feel completely ready to go, like I could sit down and answer a hundred emails or reorganize the entire executive appointment list for the month. I actually did that last week, updated the whole calendar system we use. We just switched to this new software, and it's supposed to sync with everyone's phones automatically, but half the time it doesn't update the time zones correctly when the VP travels. He went to Tokyo last month and the calendar kept scheduling his meetings for 3:00 AM local time. 

Tokyo seems like such a fascinating city, though. I watched this documentary about their subway system, and it is incredibly efficient. The trains arrive exactly on the second. Not like the transit here, where you're lucky if the bus shows up within a twenty-minute window. I was waiting in the rain on Tuesday for the express bus, and this car drove by and splashed this huge puddle right onto my slacks. I had to go to the dry cleaners on my lunch break. They have this amazing little bakery right next to the dry cleaners, though, and they make these almond croissants that are just... incredible. They have that powdered sugar on top that gets everywhere if you breathe too hard while you're eating it. I always end up looking like I've been dusted with snow. But anyway, yeah, sleep. I just haven't been sleeping much, but I feel totally energized and ready to work anyway.

inference.note: Added F31.9 because the patient now reports markedly decreased need for sleep (2–3 hours) without fatigue and feeling energized/ready to work, which raises concern for bipolar spectrum rather than unipolar depression/adjustment disorder.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the decreased need for sleep occurs as part of an abnormally elevated or expansive mood, which would help distinguish bipolar disorder from depressive or adjustment disorders.
doctor.question: During those nights when you sleep only a few hours and still feel energized, do you also feel unusually upbeat or excited?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I have stretches where I feel unusually upbeat and sure everything is clicking, then a tiny change like someone moving a meeting can make me sharp with people in a way that surprises me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I feel unusually upbeat or excited during periods of decreased sleep, which corresponds to the symptom of elevated mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I do. I get these stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, you know? Like everything is just clicking perfectly. Speaking of clicking, I actually just bought one of those mechanical keyboards for my desk at work. The sound the keys make is so satisfying, but Greg in IT says it's too loud. Greg collects vintage typewriters, actually. He brought in this beautiful old Underwood model last week to show me. It weighed an absolute ton, just solid iron. 

My grandfather used to have this huge iron anvil in his garage when I was a kid because he used to do farrier work, shaping horseshoes. Horses are such incredible animals, but I can't really be around them because I'm terribly allergic to hay. My eyes just swell up like balloons. I went on a haunted hayride once in middle school and ended up having to sit in the first aid tent with ice packs on my face the whole night while my friends got to go through the corn maze. Corn mazes are so much fun, except when it gets muddy... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought completely. What did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling upbeat. So, yeah, I'll feel really great and on top of the world, but then the weird thing is, a tiny change—like if someone just reschedules a meeting or moves something on the calendar—can suddenly make me get really sharp with people. It's in a way that honestly kind of surprises me, just how quickly I snap over something so small.

inference.note: Added evidence for bipolar spectrum: decreased need for sleep, increased energy, upbeat mood, distractibility/tangentiality, and irritability during energized periods. This makes F31.9 the leading diagnosis and rules against F43.23 as primary.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the energized, upbeat periods include increased goal-directed activity, which would help distinguish bipolar disorder from a depressive episode alone.
doctor.question: During those energized periods, do you find yourself taking on a lot more projects or getting much more done than usual?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity
target_item.manifestation: During those stretches I start rebuilding work templates, making care plans, emailing relatives, and reorganizing files all at once, like sitting still would mean I’m dropping the ball.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I take on more projects or get more done than usual during my energized periods, which directly addresses the symptom of increased goal-directed activity.

patient.answer:
Yeah, absolutely. During those stretches, I just start doing everything. I'll be rebuilding all the work templates, making up these elaborate care plans, emailing relatives I haven't spoken to in months, and reorganizing all my files all at the same time. It's like... if I sit still for even a second, I feel like I'm dropping the ball on something. 

Speaking of balls, I actually signed up for a local bocce ball league last spring. It was supposed to be this fun, relaxing thing on Thursday nights, but some of the guys take it so seriously. There's this one guy, Frank, who brings his own custom-made resin bocce balls in this velvet-lined wooden case. He acts like we're playing in the World Cup or something. I mean, I like sports, but I prefer things you can do at your own pace, like golf. My uncle used to take me golfing when I was a teenager. He had this old set of clubs that were practically antiques. He swore by his 9-iron, said it was the only club he ever really needed. He actually used it to chase a raccoon out of his garage once. The raccoon had gotten into a bag of dog food and made this enormous mess everywhere. Dog food smells so bad when it gets wet, doesn't it? I don't even own a dog, I have a cat, a little tabby named Barnaby. He's very finicky about his food, he'll only eat the pate kind, never the chunks in gravy... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, taking on projects. Yeah, I just do a ton of things all at once, like I can't stop moving or I'll fall behind.

inference.note: Episodic decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased goal-directed activity, and distractibility support bipolar disorder and rule against a purely depressive episode.
